A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Causally Reliable Concept Bottleneck Models. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite appendix reorganization and the added checklist in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, causal graph discovery, intervention, debiasing, and fairness experiments in Section 5 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and reports additional prompting, sample-size, and graph-corruption results in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The encoder, graph-construction pipeline, adaptive structural equations, and training objective are retained. Hypernetwork renames the existing neural meta-model. The corrected exclusion of X-ray anomalies in Appendix D matches the ancestor-selection rule and exclusion already stated in v2, rather than establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five Bayesian-network datasets, cMNIST, CelebA, CUBC, and SIIM-Pneumothorax, including the existing debiasing and fairness tasks. The added studies vary sample sizes, prompting, and model graph configurations within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Table 9 adds GPT-5 to the graph-refinement comparison alongside GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini. The prediction baselines and the GES, PC, FGES, and LLM/RAG discovery comparators remain unchanged. Concept Graph Models are newly discussed but are not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: v3 introduces substantial evaluation sweeps: four prompting strategies around fixed GES graphs, sample sizes from 100 to 10,000, and graph perturbation or flattening proportions from 0.05 to 1.0. These are added protocols; the existing dataset splits, preprocessing, optimizer, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's discovery-method, LLM, RAG, and true-versus-learned-graph comparisons, v3 adds sample-size sensitivity, random edge corruption, and progressive graph-flattening analyses. It substantially expands the LLM ablation to examine prompting and adds CUB panels to the existing decomposition of interventional accuracy.

E5.justification: Table 9 newly reports uncertainty across three runs instead of point estimates. The checklist clarifies that uncertainty denotes two standard errors, and Figure 12's stated multiplier changes from 1.96 to 2. However, the checklist's blanket five-seed statement conflicts with the three runs reported in Tables 9, 12, and 13.

E6.justification: The main results in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged, but Table 9 is replaced by an expanded result matrix, Tables 11–13 add sample-size and graph-corruption outcomes, and Figure 12 adds CUB results. For example, new Table 11 reports Insurance graph errors decreasing from 47 at 100 samples to 18 at 10,000. These substantially expand the reported evidence rather than demonstrate a version-to-version performance gain.

T1.justification: The SCM definitions, likelihood derivation, custom structural Hamming penalties, and Theorem D.1 with its proof are retained. Displaying the previously inline SCM equation and clarifying variable notation do not introduce new mathematical results or assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a causal concept bottleneck and automated construction pipeline, comparable predictive accuracy, improved interventions, debiasing, and fairness. The expanded appendix supplies additional evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds the interpretation that effective background knowledge can compensate for limited data and connects the corruption results to robustness against graph misspecification. It also discusses robustness across prompting strategies. Section 6 retains the existing limitations concerning knowledge quality, scalability, and encoder distribution shifts.

D1.justification: The new checklist supplies dataset-license information and states that CBM and CEM were implemented from scratch. Conversely, v3 removes v2's direct repository URL, retaining references to supplementary code and YAML configurations. The principal implementation, training, and hardware details are unchanged; removal of the link does not establish removal of the repository itself.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion of Concept Graph Models and references concerning hypernetworks, prompting, intervention learning, and causal-discovery software. Section 4.2 more explicitly positions the contribution as integrating existing prerequisites into an automated pipeline. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order are preserved. Changes include the hypernetwork terminology, explanatory corrections in the SCM and Asia examples, localized appendix rewrites and reordering, a more complete contents list, the NeurIPS checklist, and author/conference information.

P2.justification: Table 9 becomes a substantially larger table organized by LLM and prompting strategy, and Tables 11–13 are added. Figure 7 corrects the X-ray prediction branch, Figure 12 gains CUB panels and rearranges existing panels, and Table 8 reorders its metric blocks. These are substantive display additions and revisions beyond pagination changes.

improvement.justification: The expanded LLM/prompt comparison and new sample-size and corruption studies strengthen understanding of dependencies that v2 tested only partially. Correcting the Asia example also improves clarity. The gain is limited: corruption tests assess predictive accuracy rather than intervention reliability, while conflicting run-count statements and removal of the direct code link weaken reporting and reproducibility information.
